entries.description: Add api/lib/media/listing-index.js — GET /api/media/index (already committed in routes/media.js) imports it

NAME and WORK links in transcripts (Chad 10-22) — a links stage after quotes resolves the mentions the copy-edit pass returns: people through the biography set (names + aliases, then the identity lookup index; one unambiguous person or nothing) → /biography/<id>; works through the document finder by title variants (a derivative work never matches) → the canonical copy by the link policy (OceanLibrary first, English first), a named chapter through the section index; confidence ≥ 0.8, first mention per subheader section; the spoken words are the anchor (transcript.md, page.html, the item page; name/work clicks navigate, quoted words still play); links.json + transcript.json + media_links (migration 166, repo replaceMediaLinks). Remastering capped on tower (≤ 4 threads per run, ≤ 2 runs, nice 19; plan §12 thread budget)

The copy-edit pass runs on the Sonnet-tier role (Chad 10-22: choose on quality) — pilot comparison, 5.3 audio hours, same whole-talk context: Sonnet 209 substantive fixes vs Haiku 161, precision on a 25-edit read 24/25 vs 25/25, seeded checklist 28/38 applied + 8 flagged vs 31/38 + 2, $0.23 vs $0.024 per audio hour; a respelt or recapitalised word keeps its own comma/full stop; homophone/spelling spans up to four words ("only foreigner of" → "only forerunner of" was refused)

Faithfulness check aligns in order (resync on 3 matching words, case/punctuation edits are not content) — the time-only mapping raised false alarms where ASR segments overlap; one rule for the guard and the check: more words than heard only when it sounds like the whole of what was heard ('Sogefendik' → 'Shoghi Effendi' yes; 'Robart' → 'John Robarts' no). Audit of all 33 processed items: 3 insertions, all by the name pass ('(Vol II)', two added first names), none by the copy-edit. Whisper prompt leads with the English terms talks use and Whisper mishears (Forerunner, Will and Testament, World Order, Covenant, Bayán, Nabíl’s Narrative)

FAITHFULNESS enforced (Chad 10-22: '(Vol II)' hallucinated — the most serious kind) — after the name pass and after the copy-edit, every edited region is aligned by time to the ASR's own words and anything that adds to what was heard (extra words, brackets, digits, volume numbers) is reverted to the heard words; counts per stage in meta.faithfulness and insertions_reverted in the quality report; audit script over the archive files (scripts/media/audit-insertions.mjs). The copy-edit pass now reads ~12-minute chunks with neighbouring paragraphs as context, framed with speaker/title/date, and uses the model's own knowledge of Bahá'í names, works and Shoghi Effendi's transliteration (kind 'name', same guard, never more words than heard); it also returns the works and people the talk names (mentions) for the link stage; media-clean-strong role (Sonnet tier) for the model comparison. Remaster A/B script (original / smart EQ / Resemble Enhance / VoiceFixer, loudness-matched, measured)

The name pass never adds words (Chad 10-22: 'Nabips Narrative (Vol II)' — the ASR had heard "Nabeel's narrative" correctly; the name pass swapped in a junk graph title the vocabulary held) — graph names enter the vocabulary without descriptive parentheticals, capitalised parentheticals become aliases, names with digits/volumes/brackets are dropped; the guard refuses any correction with more words than were heard (one garbled word may become a two-word name) or new brackets/digits/volume numbers; Nabíl’s Narrative in the curated core

The citation IS the link (Chad 10-22: 'Don't show a reference and then a separate link read in context… just link the reference text') — breakouts on /media/<slug> and page.html link '— <author, work>' to the canonical passage; the bare ↗ after a quoted span is gone (the quoted words already link there); the photo credit links as 'Photo of <speaker>: <credit>' instead of 'source'; admin report title links instead of 'open'; test guards the media templates against generic anchor text. Deploy (frontend + Contents panel for topic subheaders)

Topic SUBHEADERS (Chad 10-22) — a headings stage after describe: the media-headings role proposes a statement or a question the talk raises at each shift of subject; a guard keeps those ≥ 2 min apart that share content words with the section they open; stored in transcript.json as kind 'heading' (source generated, model, #slug), markdown headings in transcript.md (no times: not a moment in the recording), anchored h2 + contents list in page.html, Contents panel + deep links on the item page (no word spans: click-to-play, highlight and ranges skip them). Trial: 11–14 per 46-min talk, ~$0.003 each. media-item takes ids (or 'done') and redo (re-run only the named stages; dropped on resume)
Deploy 2.187.728 (media portraits via the image worker, hidden copy-edit words, full playback, quality badge, /admin/media)

Quality surfaces (Chad 10-22) — /admin/media: the repair list grouped by fix chain (hours, summed priority), all graded recordings with a grade filter, and one recording's full report (each dimension's grade, measured values and fix, the chain with CPU cost, low-confidence spans); a small 'audio <grade> · <issue>' badge on the item page with the per-dimension grades on hover

Concept cross-linking — phase 1 related talks (Media vectors) + texts discussed (quote/CR links); phases 2–3 wait for the concept-extraction pipeline (concept tags, concept pages listing talks, concept map, entity → biography links)

Quality GRADE in the pipeline (Chad 10-22) — a stage after archive measures the original (bandwidth, SNR + DNSMOS BAK + mains-hum lines, clipping, dropouts + NISQA discontinuity, LUFS / loudness range, speaking pitch, DNSMOS + NISQA MOS) and after transcription adds intelligibility (probe log-prob, low-confidence spans) and per-speaker levels; a per-dimension report each with its grade and fix, overall grade, primary/secondary issues, the fix chain in processing order with CPU cost, and priority = (5 − grade) × speaker importance; repair list grouped by chain, listing filters, media-grade back-fill job (migration 165; thresholds in plan §10)

An item's own picture is only its generated tile — the per-item photo search found namesakes ("Chad Jones" the economist, a "Bob Harris"); the speaker's portrait record is shown in its place; the catalogue always records the speaker key
An Apify run's cost is its usageTotalUsd (it already includes the actor's per-event charges)

The copy-edit pass (Chad 10-22) — a new stage after the name corrections: the media-clean role proposes kind-tagged edits (filler, stutter, repeat loop, hallucination, spelling, homophone, capitalisation, punctuation, broken word) and a guard accepts only what it can verify (never a paraphrase; low confidence only flagged); dropped words are hidden with their time, so click-to-play and the highlight stay aligned; the verbatim layer and the full log are kept in transcript.json

The full YouTube run (Chad 10-22: "go ahead") — audio by the first route that works: free yt-dlp with a PO token, then Titan Network, then Seemuapps (Apify, APIFI_API; the file taken at once and checksummed, the run's cost recorded on the item); metadata from oEmbed when yt-dlp is refused; the route, checksum and every failed attempt kept in meta.source.download
40 speaker portraits found on the web (Wilmette Institute, bahai.media, Commons, Bahai Library, BahaiTeachings, Burhan Institute) — each checked to be the person, page and host credit kept

YouTube audio via a PO token (bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider, script mode — nothing listening, no cookies or account); archive.org alternate-source finder for the YouTube targets; speaker keys ignore initials and parentheticals; Bahaipedia aliases for portraits found under another spelling

Everything plays FULL from our own copy (Chad 10-22: "everything should be local. Youtube is only for linking out") — default level full for every source, a media-playback job sets the catalogue and re-renders the published pages; channel records still lower one source; spend entry for the $25 YouTube download API test
The player header's portrait size computed in the script (a {@const} under <figure> broke the build)

One canonical portrait per speaker (media_speakers, migration 164; keyed by folded name, linked to the graph person) — the biography portrait first, else found on the web (Bahaipedia/bahai.media with credit and source from the file page, Wikidata/Commons and Wikipedia only when the person is a Bahá'í; never a namesake or a group photo); the master stored once in the cdn-assets R2 bucket like the biography portraits and every size served by the image service with the biography helpers and fo-face (listing tile, player header, search avatar, OG 1200×630); credit shown on the item page; media-speakers job and the thumb stage for new items
Status — full local run queued (402 recordings, 31 duplicates), post-fix correction sample 20/20
Morning status — pilot results (enhancement by measurement, quote/CR precision read by hand, corrections, cost, speed), live links, the full run, YouTube block, decisions

Transcription and diarization run DETACHED — the boss ASR job (gate verbs start/poll/fetch/cancel) and the tower diarization keep running through a drain and the resumed stage re-attaches (meta.asr_job, the pid file); deploys every few minutes had kept killing a 15-minute stage
2.187.727 — the /media pages (listing + player) and the Worker's R2 cache for media files

Interpreted talks detected on twelve 12-second windows (two languages each heard twice) — six 30 s windows heard only the dominant language in Chad's English + Romanian talk; a file-name title that names nothing ("01 (thursday)", "Class 5") gives way to the recording's own subject

Proposed corrections trimmed to the name itself (context words copied on both sides, swallowed common words, a name inside a longer span) — on the 2nd Grossmann run 50 of 57 refused edits become right fixes and no spoken word is lost; the prompt asks for the name only; speaker photos: Wikidata searched without diacritics, the Bahá'í religion claim accepted, Commons by file name as fallback
Storage plan rollout status (R1–R8 done, R5 re-measure pending); backup check timings as measured
The vocabulary's entity names come from LIVE graph entities by importance (the first build filtered on religion/mention_count, which these records do not carry, and found none)

A failing recording is recorded on its item (admin status, morning summary) instead of raising an ops alert mail per file; ordered YouTube queue (881 talks: curated → single-speaker channels → other Hands/UHJ); status update

Vectors-backup never blocks indexing — own 'backup' lane; a store whose writer runs (or starts mid-copy) is skipped for the next run, not waited on; big stores verified by header + page count + size + random rows vs source (seconds) instead of a full quick_check (240 GB on the HDD fell to ~1 MB/s after 4 h); a complete .partial is adopted, never copied again (completion marker, or header/size/source-unchanged for older copies); failed copies kept as .bad
A between-stages yield also records the stage it stops before (so the resumed run skips its from/reslug)
A resumed media-item run continues at its saved stage and never redoes its from / reslug (a from:web run redid web on every resume; a resumed reslug would have deleted its own new folder)

The correction guard keeps every spoken word — an edit whose first or last word is a common English word the term lacks is refused (pilot: "Shogu Effendi told" → "Shoghi Effendi" dropped "told"; 4 such of 74 model edits, all now refused, no correct fix lost)
AAC clips (and the .m4a file) where the browser cannot play Ogg Opus (older Safari), in the site player and the standalone page

No orphaned children on a drain — the transcribe stage waits for both its children (allSettled) and every live child is killed when the process exits (10-22 00:13 an ssh to boss outlived its drained service); the media service gets its own small entry (api/workers/media-worker.js) so other services' deploys do not drain a transcription

Interpreted talks found by an UNFORCED language ID on six excerpts (the probe forced the hinted language, so Furútan's Persian+English talk read as English-only); the majority language when one; short misheard names are suspects too ("Beloved Bob" → the Báb)

Waveform normalisation looped instead of spreading 220k values (a 92-minute talk overflowed the stack and failed its web stage); a speaker written in the file name stands when the naming model leaves it out

Tower-side media processes capped at 8 threads (measured: diarization at 12 threads pushed search p90 to 3.8 s / max 5.3 s; at 8 search stayed at median 1.6 s, p90 2.1 s); the transcript completes a surname-only speaker; search-latency probe (fresh queries, API client)

YouTube rate limit (tower got 429 after the target-list discovery) holds the item without a failure alert and starts no YouTube work for a 6-hour cool-down (local files go on), then one polite retry; yt-dlp uses deno (user space) for YouTube's player; transcript search hits only at timed paragraphs

Dewey's media drop folder is watched (a dropped file queues the pipeline); diarization fragments folded into their neighbours (the pilot lecture came back as 94 voices) and unnamed voices get no label; status draft

Cross-references only from canonical works (book authority ≥ 7, most authoritative yes wins — the pilot linked a visitor's account); a clipped name is offered its full form ("Baola" → Bahá’u’lláh, the pilot corrected it to Bahá)

Drain-aware media pipeline — every long child process (ffmpeg, DeepFilterNet, ASR on boss, diarization) is killed the moment its service drains and the run yields with { resume: { id, stage } } (finished stages are the checkpoint; the gate on boss kills its work when the ssh session goes); diarization runs on tower beside the boss ASR; media jobs move to their own service siftersearch-media (OPS_ONLY) so a transcription never parks the reports lanes (10-21 watch finding)

Diarization on English speaker embeddings (wespeaker, threshold 0.7: a 92-min Q&A → 12 voices, the zh model gave 131); boss always runs this checkout's media_tool.py (installed through the gate); any two languages in the probe → interpreted mode (Chad's talks are English + Romanian)

Search hits on a transcript link to the recording (▶ Listen → /media/<slug>?p=<paragraph_index>, mapped at ingest); force-reslug of a pilot item retires its transcript doc; diarize subcommand + English speaker embeddings (threshold tuning); pilot review script (reads the archive folders only)
Add single-speaker channels and Persian-name searches to the YouTube talk targets

Vectors-backup finishes the store in progress through an update drain (SIGHUP) and yields between stores; only a stop aborts — SQLite backup cannot resume, and another agent's deploy discarded 101 of 240 GB (10-21)

/media listing + /media/<slug> player (click a word to play, paragraph play buttons, FAB, follow-scroll, playing-word highlight token, ?t= ranges, Media Session, quotes + cross-reference breakouts); YouTube items default to full playback with a per-channel permission record (Chad 10-21), download off; Dewey add_media tool; linked originals never chmodded (a hard link shares the source's inode); the model's naming wins over folder guesses; reslug for unpublished items; Python tools forced to CPU
YouTube target list of talks by Hands of the Cause, UHJ members and the curated Sacred Traditions sheet

Media library pipeline — per-item archive (original linked read-only, light/DeepFilterNet enhancement chosen by ASR probe), WhisperX on boss via a forced-command key (RTF 0.06 vs 0.36 on tower) with diarization (sherpa-onnx) and an interpreted-talk mode, vocabulary-guarded name corrections (Haiku role, diff logged, never rewording), quotations → SourceHunt + citation gates, attributed teachings → verified cross-references, transcript.md (para ids + t0/t1) ingested as collection Media with content_source_links, standalone page.html player, Opus/AAC + waveform; media_items/media_channels (migration 163), /api/media (listing, transcript search, Range files, signed ≤180 s clips), ops jobs media-scan/media-item/media-vocab (lane media), Worker R2 cache for versioned media files

Media library plan — per-item archive, enhancement by measurement, WhisperX + vocabulary corrections, quote linking via SourceHunt, /media pages, Worker R2 cache, rights; spend allowance for the pilot (≤ $20/day to 11-05, approved by Chad 10-21)
Meilisearch retired (CLAUDE.md, scripts/CLAUDE.md); plan §6.6 phase 0 — temp_path must stay on the RAM disk, usable hot capacity ≈ 22 GB, crash-test results

Qdrant-hot temp_path stays on the RAM disk — CLI snapshot recovery renames temp → storage and cannot cross filesystems (every restore panicked in the tower crash test); indexer keeps RAM-disk free ≥ hot data so snapshot temp files fit
A snapshot rewrites every segment.json, so counting it made each flush mark the next one dirty (measured on tower) — dirty detection ignores segment.json

Phase 0 hot layer — new phrase points go to phrases_hot on the RAM-disk Qdrant (qdrant-hot :6335) while phrases on /fast stays frozen; search merges main + hot (hot down = main only); phrases writes mirrored; coverage counts both; units marked upserted=2 + phrase-hot-reconcile re-sends what a crash lost (queued at every indexer start); RAM-full guard; units at phase-0 values (44G, snapshots on /crutch) (storage plan §6.6)

RAM-disk kit (deploy/qram units, scripts/ops/qram.mjs flush/restore + tests) and NUT kit (deploy/nut, upssched powerdown hook, ups-mail) — committed, NOT installed; plan §1.1 UPS test procedure, §6.4 install steps

Retire Meilisearch — MEILISEARCH_ENABLED=false (no client, no startup spawn, no outbox deletes), health follows Qdrant, system-checks no longer probes :7700, daily backup skips the Meili rsync, cache prewarm no longer gated on Meili, Meili-only paths return empty (storage plan R8)

Vectors-backup job — online SQLite backup of the three paid vectors.db stores to /tank/sifter/backups/vectors, paced in a nice-19 worker thread, copy verified (page count, size, quick/integrity check) before rotation; index lane, refuses while a writer runs, yields to drains (storage plan R1)
MP44 specs (TLC, 2,000 TBW, HMB), 7910 slot map (Slot1 Gen3 x4 CPU1 free), drive install steps, keep GTX 1070 / pull K4000
Storage wear + RAM plan — measured baseline (NVMe 6.2 TB/day 10-13..20 → 0.09 after MEILI_WRITES=off), RAM budget, RAM disk + flush, per-device layout, UPS sizing
SearchGrounded reads bound claims once per process, not a LIKE scan per cluster
Anís overview off the event loop; docs listing counts once and pages by id

Paragraph-authors refuses without ids unless all:true; saved labels read once (an existsSync per sort comparison over 57,903 books froze the reports event loop — 'silent', cancel and drain unheard, 10-21)
Paragraph-authors checkpoints every 20 windows and yields to a drain INSIDE a book, resuming there (10-21: a 15,600-paragraph Bahá'í World volume held the reports service draining 70+ min)
Db-ship's /tank copy takes no auto-snapshots (inherited from tank, they break incrementals); system-checks reads the newest SHIP snapshot (paged CRITICAL on a 'frequent' auto-snap)
Doc-overlap report — per section, paragraphs held word for word elsewhere (Compilation of Compilations: extract what is missing, then retire)
Reparse flag — a parser change (Ibid expansion) reaches unchanged files; ingest-files { reparse }
Ibid. expanded to the reference it stands for — compilation trailers and footnotes (Chad 10-21: 'Ibid does not work for RAG'); library files keep their wording

'(Ibid.)' trailers inherit the previous trailer's writer; a trailer ending ')
' before its attribute tail is still a trailer (10-21: ~110 Lights of Guidance quotations had no author)

Db-ship never touches the 03:00 backup's snapshot; system-checks 'DB ship to /tank' freshness; prune-db-snapshots retired (db-ship keeps one SSD base). Plan: citations render as markdown links, DB stores the source record
Db-ship — hourly ZFS snapshot on the SSD, incremental send to /tank, SSD keeps one base (Chad 10-21: fast backup then migrate off SSD; same for /faster)
Chad's 10-21 decisions — on-behalf letters are Shoghi Effendi's; page cites link by quoted text
An SLP wait yields to the drain — job id kept on the item, resumed on the next start (10-21: a 2-hour OCR wait held the reports service draining 1 h+, parking citation linking and intake)

Claims layer gets a 1.5 s grace after the passages — a cold claim worker after a restart held people-ish searches ~10 s (10-21: 10.6 s for 'the role of the Hands of the Cause today', passages ready at 1.5 s)
Roadmap served stale while it refreshes; telemetry's hourly call waits 90 s — /grounding/status timed out (20 s) on cold recomputes after restarts (gateway timeouts 10-20, 10-21)

/grounding/exhaustion serves a background-refreshed snapshot (pending right after a restart); system-checks treats pending as unknown — after deploys the cold 600-book walk took >30 s and paged CRITICAL 'nothing queued' (10-21 12:49)
_add-anyway overrides an earlier 'already held' decline (Egea's 'Abdu'l-Bahá in the West was declined as held in Promulgation — it quotes it, it is not it)

Hidden traditions — meta.yaml hidden: true ('Other': works spanning traditions, related ideas, contrasting beliefs) are searchable but never shelved or listed (shelves, library religions, public API) (Chad 10-21)
Paced by the clock — overnight 2 at a time, by day one at a time with a 30 s pause; a sweep's back-to-back holdings checks drove Qdrant reads to ~300 MB/s and search to 4–14 s (paused: 2–4 s)
Daily backup runs at idle CPU+IO priority (nice 19, ionice idle) — at normal priority its quick_check took search to 39 s; idled live, search back to 0.3–0.6 s
Daily backup at 03:00 local — tower cron runs on MST, so '0 10' (meant as 10 UTC) ran the 58 GB copy + quick_check at 10 AM, slowing search to 2–7 s every morning
One hunt at a time + 1.5 s pause — two concurrent hunts took search from 1.6 s to 5–11 s (10-21 09:49)
Fall back to the next considered candidate that is the writer's own work; approved spend for citation linking (Chad 10-21)

The SOURCE decides whose words — a compilation's voice tag is only a hint (sample 2 rejected Hidden Words / Messages to America matches); source must be one of the four writers' own non-compilation work

Gates from the 10-21 sample — hunt only real quotations (≥12 words, not metadata/citation fragments, the writer's own voice) in library/OceanLibrary compilations; accept only the writer's OWN work (not mirrors, not secondary books) with verbatim or ≥0.3 shared wording; rejects counted by reason

Source-links-build — compilation quotes of Bahá'u'lláh/the Báb/'Abdu'l-Bahá/Shoghi Effendi → their source via SourceHunt (own work first, compilation excluded; verbatim vs translation); dry run default, limit, drain-resumable, own 'linking' lane (Chad 10-21)
Source-link-coverage report — per compilation, paragraphs voicing Bahá'u'lláh/the Báb/'Abdu'l-Bahá/Shoghi Effendi and how many link to their source (citation plan step 0, Chad 10-21)
One letter, one answer — a range found as chapter and dated message listed once
Every citation a real link — detect → resolve (source links, refs, letter lookup, pagination, phrase) → linkFor → render → measure (Chad 10-21)

Letter lookup — an author's letters as books, chapters and dated messages (work_letters, migr 162; letters-index job; GET /api/library/letters?date&title&book → canonical link + reader range). Timeline benchmark: 97/103 top-1 (rest = same-date twins / sub-section). schema-contract test now parses single-line CREATEs (Chad 10-21)

/document/:id generates the slug when none is stored (OceanLibrary canonicals — every Anís/Jafar citation to them landed on /library/); a duplicate holding a slug yields to its canonical on the page (Bahá’í Administration served dup #16278 not #20880)
Doc-corrections job — a person's author/translator corrections through docs-repo (dry run first); docs-repo setDocTranslators (Chad 10-21)
Settled-book memo 6 h (30 min = the health probe's interval, so every /grounding/exhaustion probe walked cold, 26 s → gateway 30 s timeout 10-20 23:49); overlapping exhaustion calls share one walk
A writer freeze is CRITICAL only within the last 3 h — a fixed 6-hour-old 46.7 s write re-paged as critical while ageing out of the 24 h window
Ingest folder _add-anyway/ — a person's decision adds a file the check calls held (the library copy is an excerpt; pilgrim notes held at 30–77%) (Chad 10-20)
Prune keeps 6 hourly + 3 daily DB snapshots on /fast, hourly cron (Chad 10-20: 24 hourlies pinned 62 GB, /fast 90%)
Failed service probes report why (timeout/DNS/TLS/refused) — the 10-20 18:00 'Public API (tunnel): status 0' alert could not be traced
Review popup on the solid surface (surface-1 is 80% alpha — the chat showed through the document)
RTF/Word/WordPerfect/ODT/EPUB originals readable in the Review popup (server-converted, sanitised, sandboxed) + 'View it' on offer cards — read before Add it / Not this one (Chad 10-20)
Read roots include Public/Ocean-books and Public/pilgrim-notes (Chad's 10-20 sweeps were refused 400 'outside the folders Dewey may read'); test pin SEARCH_VERSION 2026-10-20.4
Migration 161 unreachable (CURRENT_VERSION not bumped) → every holdings check 500'd 'no such table: dewey_checks'; the memo read is now an optimisation — a failure is a miss, never a failed check

Holdings-check memo — file content sha256 → last verdict (dewey_checks, migr 161); the same book checked again (renamed, moved) answers instantly; held stands while its document is live, other verdicts 7 days; ?fresh=1 (Chad 10-20)

MEILI_WRITES=off — stop pushing paragraphs/HyPE/mentions/aliases to Meilisearch (retirement step 5); it was the largest I/O on /fast (20 MB/s r, 13 MB/s w) though search reads only Qdrant, while writes took 9–27 s and hydration 2–6 s. Dirty rows settled; removals still reach Qdrant

Stamp-voices/stamp-site yield to a drain and resume where they stopped — #973 held the indexer in 'draining' for hours; a yielding job's resume params are saved on the run (saveResume) so the requeue continues, not restarts

Two 30 s main-thread reads behind 10-20 gateway timeouts — library slug fallback read every docs row (now matching collections only, via docs-repo.docsForPathSlugs); planExhaustion prose check GROUP BY over ~600 books' paragraphs → EXISTS per book

Settled plan books are not re-probed — refill (every 3 min) and planExhaustion walked all ~600 finished books on the API main thread each time (5–8 s resume-stage spikes); null answers remembered 30 min, each probe yields the loop
The grounding exhaustion probe gets 30 s (it checks every plan book, 5–6 s) — the default 8 s timeout made an exhausted plan a CRITICAL 'nothing queued' alarm
Rights classes per Chad's rule — Writings, institutional and anything online are shareable in full; only privately published books not found online are restricted

Rights — the old encumbered flag is overly broad (collection/religion defaults); restrict only on per-document evidence, unknown stays shareable and goes to review; measure current breadth first (Chad 10-20)
Rights replaces the encumbered flag — per-document class + evidence, one servingPolicy module; encumbered derived then retired (Chad 10-20)
Rights classification — shareable in full vs copyrighted (encumbered) for every document; Dewey sets it at intake, backfill for the library (Chad 10-20)
Keep only the newest 3 daily DB snapshots on /fast (Chad 10-20) — 31 dailies pinned ~60 GB of churned DB blocks and the pool hit 96%; full daily copies live on /tank
Coverage one pass
Book coverage (prose/disamb/hyped/extracted/hypeable) is ONE pass over the book's rows, not five COUNT subqueries — grounding:resume-stage took 8.8 s on the API main thread for large books
Site DBs — the per-site store already exists for site-only (getSiteDb); step 2 extends it

Stamp-site job — every scraped site's Qdrant points carry `site` (payload only, by doc-id batches, keyword index) so site scopes filter in Qdrant and hits can hydrate from per-site stores (planning/site-databases-plan.md step 1)
One database per scraped site (bahai-library, oceanoflights, bahaiteachings); OceanLibrary.com stays in the primary DB as the canonical English collection (Chad 10-20)
With no --qdrant flag the type battery uses the server's default search config — it sent qdrant:false and silently measured the legacy Meili path

Spending Chad approved is not an alarm — the 24 h spend alert fires only above the base threshold plus the active approved allowances (data/approved-spend.json: doctrinal index 00/day, authorship 0/day, until 10-27)
The authoritative pass runs only in a Bahá'í-scoped search again — unscoped it displaced other traditions (battery 66 → 60: karma, wu wei, nirvana, fasting). SEARCH_VERSION bumped

Under SEARCH_QDRANT=only hybridSearch / keywordSearch / searchHypeQuestions answer from Qdrant (authority-ranked multiIndexSearch with Meili off; BM25 for keyword mode) — every direct Meili caller (public /v1/search, keyword route, chat, deep research, grounding counts) moves at once; site-only scopes stay on Meili for now (Chad 10-20: retire Meilisearch)
Meili retirement — direct search callers inventoried; documents/deep_research write-only

The authoritative pass also runs in UNSCOPED searches (most readers never pick a tradition — 'detachment from the world' found no Hidden Words) as candidates; the Bahá'í tier weights still apply only in a Bahá'í search, so interfaith slots stay fair. SEARCH_VERSION bumped

Qdrant ranks alone (SEARCH_QDRANT=only) — with doctrinal-authority fusion the type battery scores 66/83 vs 63/83 on Meili, p50 1.6 s vs 4.4 s, p95 4.2 s vs 18 s (Chad 10-20: retire Meilisearch). Meili still receives writes; rollback = phrase,keyword
Person-search claims (bioSearch hay_folded LIKE scan, 5.8 s) run on the claim-search worker thread's own connection — no longer on the API's event loop

Each writer cycle leaves a phase breadcrumb (/tmp/siftersearch-writer-phase.json) and the watchdog logs it when it restarts the writer — a 45 s freeze at 07:08 left no trace (killed before any slow-query log); the watchdog never restarts twice within 2 min (the old writer is still draining)

Bahá'í doctrinal tiers and the authoritative pass apply only inside a Bahá'í-scoped search — unscoped interfaith queries ('what is nirvana', Qur'anic patience, karma) were handed Bahá'í texts first; across traditions each passage ranks by its own authority within its tradition's slots. Meilisearch retirement plan — inventory of indexes and callers; Qdrant-only battery loses famous passages to secondary copies (no authority fusion) → authority-aware fusion first

Concept_entities full rebuild

Phelps' provisional English renderings of the tablets → library files (Tablet Translations/Stephen Phelps (provisional)/<author>/<PIN>.md), labelled provisional-phelps, credited to the tablet's author, linked to the original by PIN; official translations and unsegmented texts skipped (Chad 10-19)
Reads in batch loops (indexer, reports-carry, embedding, audit) are not 'blocking' — no request waits on them

Person search off the serving thread — entitySearch scanned+folded all entity_claims per call (10–13 s, ~200×/day on api and anis main threads: the slow-query emails); claims now held folded on one worker thread (claim-search.js), queries scan in memory
Paragraph-authors job has a spend cap (maxLlm Haiku calls, default 20,000) — no new book past it; the rest resume next run

A process mid-reload is given its own drain time (kill_timeout) + 1 min before it pages — the writer drains its batch and took >60 s on an ordinary deploy (false critical 'siftersearch-worker stopping')
Trailer paragraphs still get the classifier's quoted voices (author stays locked) — the 20804 dry run lost ~1,000 quoted voices by skipping them
Keyword-fill points carry voices_fold too — a gap-filled paragraph quoting the Báb is findable by 'the Báb' at once, not after the next stamp-voices pass

Attribution trailers are EVIDENCE in the paragraph-authors job — a quotation followed by '(From a letter written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi …)' takes that writer (basis trailer) before the classifier runs; pandoc attribute tails stripped (Lights of Guidance quotations were labelled the compiler)

A service mid-reload (launching/stopping) is looked at again for up to 60 s before it pages anyone — graceful deploys were false criticals; the macro-services (gateway, anis, ops, indexer, reports) are now required and watched

Every VOICE is findable by author — points carry voices_fold (the paragraph's author + every quoted voice); an author filter matches writer OR quoted voice; stamp-voices job (indexer service) stamps existing points by paragraph, payload only; keyword indexer writes it (Chad 10-19: the Báb quoted by Mázandarání answers 'what did the Báb say')

A Bahá'í compilation (author, author_2, … in the frontmatter) is credited to its compiler in the MAIN library ingester too — one shared rule (library/compilation-author.js); its copy of Lights of Guidance was 'by Bahá'u'lláh'. compilation-authors ops job finds and (with write) corrects existing library records (Chad 10-19)

Every paragraph its author, library-wide — the window classifier (v18b rules) as the 'paragraph-authors' ops job (reports service, own lane): reads via paragraphs-repo, writes through the writer with rollback, resumable per book, secondary rules for scholars/compilations; escalations on Haiku 5.5 (DeepSeek retired). Doctrine is then selected by PARAGRAPH author, not book (Chad 10-19)

Trace_source — a House letter, scholar or compilation stating a teaching is a signpost; the researcher traces it (quote links, else the closest passages of the four authoritative authors) and cites the primary passage (Chad 10-19)

Warm-ups (the ~24 s encounter query) run BEFORE listening — behind the gateway the old instance serves until 'ready', while warming after listen froze live Anís conversations (74 blocking reads in 'anis' in 3 h)
System-checks --report — the same checks as JSON, no email, no state (the agent's own periodic watch reads it)

The updater restart storm (289 restarts, every 30 s) — pm2 killed it at its 100M memory limit once it computed every service's import graph per lagging service; graphs now cached per run, limit 512M. An ecosystem.config.cjs edit touches only the apps whose own pm2 block changed (old config read from git), not every service

Authority decides — doctrinal questions answered ONLY from the Revelation and its authorised interpretation; the House only for applying the law and the administration; scholars only labelled history. The judge and the auditor score a doctrinal point rested on the House or a scholar as an authority error, not a better answer (Chad 10-19: 'an antipattern, not better'); battery --rejudge
A failed job records and logs its stack (a bare 'Request timed out' did not say which call); battery judge accepts 'Answer B' labels

From the 61-question Immerse battery — a real topic or pasted passage is never deflected as 'unclear'/'cut off'; references read in the reader's community and the present (ABS, the Nine Year Plan, the House, message paragraphs); study questions researched broadly and answered in full, organised; search API now serves only its own routes (Anís and ops via the gateway)
Macro-services behind the gateway — layout, ports, coordinator (CLAUDE.md + continuous-deploy.md)
Under pm2 cluster mode argv[1] is pm2's container — recognise the entry by pm_exec_path (the gateway never listened)

The API splits into macro-services behind a gateway — siftersearch-gateway (7839, where the tunnel points; routes by path, retries a restarting service, streams), siftersearch-api (search, 7845), siftersearch-anis (conversations/letters/reading/widget, 2 instances, 7844), siftersearch-ops (health/reports, 7843): an Anís update reloads only Anís (Chad 10-19: 3,000 readers/day, dozens of updates, no interrupted conversations). Shared runtime (api-runtime.js) + shared server (http-server.js) + route sets; every service answers /healthz; the coordinator boots each new build on a test port before any reload; stray-killer waits out the 300 s drain
A file ADDED in a deploy cannot be loaded by running code — no fallback reload for it (the new indexer entry reloaded writer, deep-research and embedding for nothing); behind-check logs quietly

INDEXING is its own macro-service (siftersearch-indexer: phrase/HyPE/concept/section vectors, BM25, coverage ledger) on a 57-file import graph with no Dewey or Anís code — other services' deploys leave it running; ops services share one runtime (drain, heartbeat, lanes, alerts); a restart requeues only ITS OWN interrupted jobs (reports used to requeue carry's live ones); the coordinator starts newly declared services (Chad 10-19)
Answers as jobs (start + poll) — no request stays open for Cloudflare's 125 s limit or a reload (40 of 61 were 524s)

A service is behind only when its heartbeat commit lags HEAD in code IT loads (not pm2's package version); a version-only package.json bump is no change; a draining service is never signalled or verified twice (frontend deploy 2.187.723: mail drafts as jobs)
Only the pm2 API reports — the updater's pre-deploy test instance inherited its name

Continuous deploy without breaking work — coordinator touches only the services a change reaches (import graph); queue services DRAIN (SIGHUP: finish the work in hand, exit, pm2 restarts on new code); API drains requests AND jobs for 300 s; long work is a JOB (Anís mail drafts: async + poll, no more 524 or per-minute recompute); every service heartbeats its version/health/work → GET /api/admin/ops/services (Chad 10-19; docs/architecture/continuous-deploy.md)

A push touching no runtime code (tests, docs, frontend, hand-run scripts) is pulled without reloading the API and writer — a script-only push killed in-flight Anís research answers with 502s (10-19); research replies get 8,000 tokens (Sonnet thinks first; 2,700 cut them off); a timed-out research round retries once and logs round + elapsed
A network failure is one answer's error, never the end of the run; results saved after every batch

--immerse runs the questions people asked bahaiwritings.app against Immerse's own answers (detailed · doctrinal · nuanced · interesting; the gap Anís left is recorded); our test addresses are audited but never alert Chad
Earlier replies are context, never audited unless the reader questions them (three 'corrections' of Lal's chart were all false)
A word study shows both measures, labelled — aligned-passage counts and CTAI's root-level counts — so an earlier root-level chart is not mistaken for an error
An earlier reply is corrected only with a passage, precisely — never called unsupported or invented (a root-wide count is a different measure, not an error)
The researcher switch never leaks into test harnesses (injected deps keep it off unless they inject a researcher)
An empty word study is about the spelling, never evidence — no disowning an earlier reply on it; candidate words are checked in the concordance in Arabic script

The researcher answers EMAIL — Haiku 5.5 plans, Sonnet 5.5 writes; battery 10-19 (10 real questions, Opus blind): mean 7.45, beat Perplexity 10/10 (old pipeline 5.0, 6/10); chat stays on the fast path

Research battery vs Perplexity (Opus judges blind); the brief's markers never reach the reader; the writer never volunteers what it could not find; well-known background (Shoghi Effendi translated Gleanings) is stated, not doubted

The researcher — Haiku 5.5 plans the research with the library's tools (search, read around, original of a passage, Shoghi Effendi's renderings, source of a quotation, web) and briefs the writer; replaces regex routing when ANIS_RESEARCH names the channel (off by default); /draft takes research + writer for the battery (Chad 10-19: 'too determinative')
A language answer never says it 'couldn't find anything'

Every Anís exchange is judged against Perplexity's answer to the same (scrubbed) question — vs_competitor better/equal/worse with what each gave; 'worse' alerts like a poor answer (Chad 10-19: always more helpful than Perplexity)

The quibble lint — a sentence correcting the reader's case endings is dropped unless they asked about grammar; a language answer never disclaims that 'the texts I can search do not settle' it (Chad 10-19)

Language questions get their own shape — answered from knowledge of the language and the passage under discussion, no padding search; authority shown by use, never described (Chad 10-19, Lal's 'fí baytihi')

Explore, never shut a question down — language knowledge (word meanings, which Arabic/Persian words carry an idea, grammar) is his to give; a reader's spelling/grammar slip is never corrected; the auditor judges exploration first and flags 'shut-down' replies (Chad 10-19, Lal's 'chamber' follow-up)
The main ingester HOLDS a file whose 'paragraph' is a whole book (>8,000 chars) even when it declares its paragraphing — nothing is cut, nothing unsegmented gets in (Chad 10-19)
Quality gate before ingestion — repair then judge; below the bar is HELD, never ingested (Chad 10-19)

A file whose row was retired as a duplicate AND soft-deleted stays retired (a forced bahai-library re-ingest would have resurrected 598 pages retired for their OceanLibrary copies); unsegmented-docs lists live documents only, deleted ones with orphaned paragraphs counted apart

Text with no sentence structure (verse lines, lists) is split at line breaks then words, never left whole; bahai-library's raw-HTML navigation table (8,538 chars on hundreds of pages) is dropped as site chrome
Sites-ingest takes a file list — re-ingest exactly the files a fix touched (dry run supported)
Letters read like Jafar's — a quotation is quoted text with its link on the work (whole passages showed as underlined link text); headings, bold, lists and rules styled inline (Chad 10-19)
Unsegmented-docs report — every live document holding a whole-book 'paragraph', surveyed in short id windows: the re-ingest list (Chad 10-19)
A whole-book 'paragraph' (unsegmented import awaiting re-ingest) is never returned as a passage — filtered before the 500-char cut hid its size

No whole-book paragraphs — the site2rag adapter split bahai-library PDF markdown only on blank lines and read one page marker a block, so a book with single newlines became ONE 'paragraph' (50k–700k chars) that polluted every search (Chad 10-19: 'Never should we search an unsegmented book … a bug in the ingester'). Every page marker starts a block; an oversized block is split on its own structure (sentence-ending line breaks, then sentence boundaries); the sites ingester REFUSES a file that still has a >8,000-char paragraph (logged, nothing indexed)

The Universal House of Justice is APPLICATION, not doctrine (Chad 10-19, per the Will and Testament: authoritative on applying Bahá'í law, not decisive on doctrine) — doctrine is the Revelation (Bahá'u'lláh, the Báb) and its authorised interpretation ('Abdu'l-Bahá, Shoghi Effendi); House passages are labelled [application] and cited after the doctrine

Within doctrine, a work the planner named for the theme leads, then relevance; the authority number only breaks ties (a loosely related Aqdas line outranked the exact Promised Day passage); the named works are searched first
The position planner gets 6000 tokens — Haiku spent all 1500 thinking and returned no text (finish 'length')
Log why the position planner returned no text
The position planner's lines are parsed through bullets, numbers and bold (a dressed reply parsed as no themes and the answer fell back); its raw text is logged when no theme parses

Position planner covers the related doctrines a scholar would cite (property as an institution, the state, taxation and the rights of subjects, trade, materialist ideologies), up to 7 themes / 20 passages; the 'kinds of authority' opening is dropped
Letters (email) and position answers get room — the 700-token chat cap cut both mid-sentence; a reply that hits the cap is logged

DOCTRINE apart from opinion in position answers (Chad 10-19: 'separate actual doctrine [from] human fad opinions … authority is everything'): only the writings of Bahá'u'lláh, the Báb, 'Abdu'l-Bahá, Shoghi Effendi and the UHJ carry the answer — a pilgrim note never, a writer's view only labelled [opinion] and set against the texts; each passage reaches the writer marked [doctrine]/[opinion] with its theme; the planner answers in lines (its JSON broke on a quoted title and the answer fell back silently)
Position research logs its themes, failures and counts (it fell back silently on tower)

POSITION questions researched theme by theme, authoritative texts first (Chad 10-19: the socialism/equality/property answer came from pilgrim notes and secondary articles — 'extremely shallow and wishy washy'): one planning call names the themes and the works that address them (where to look, never the answer); each theme searched within the Faith's texts; passages ranked Central Figures / Shoghi Effendi / UHJ first, secondary only to fill, unsegmented whole-book 'paragraphs' dropped; the reply goes theme by theme, quoting the authoritative texts, without hedging or 'the library has nothing' when passages exist. House style: authority order in every answer
The English of a quoted passage is the ORIGINAL's own linked translation (Gleanings ¶606 for Muntakhabát 136) — the phrase search's top hits were all compilations quoting it
The English of a quoted passage comes from the original's own author's work (Gleanings) before any compilation quoting it; the lookup's shortlist is 10, not 3

The English is taken from the work itself, ranked by the library's authority (not a memoir quoting it — the reply named 'Fires in Many Hearts' for Gleanings CXXXVI); a work the seeker named that the passage is not in is corrected in one gentle sentence; the 'As for the authorities behind these sources' paragraph is dropped. The auditor ALERTS Chad at once when an answer falls short (Chad 10-19: 'every single interaction with Anis should be audited immediately after for quality')

ANY quoted passage → its original (Chad 10-19: 'fix Anis'). The original-wording step knew only the Hidden Words; Lal's 'chamber' (Gleanings CXXXVI, no quotation marks, an Aqdas attribution and a P.S.) was looked up as one text and Anís answered 'I couldn't find it'. Now each passage the seeker quoted runs through the library's English→original lookup (findOriginals) and the reply is written from the English passage and its Arabic/Persian, naming where the passage actually appears

The daily digest shows her CONVERSATIONS like Jafar's — numbers, the replies the auditor flagged first (with its reasons), who asked, every question and answer as the reader saw it; the mail activity after (Chad 10-19: 'follow conversations early on to head off poor answers')
The day's conversations for the daily digest — GET /api/v1/anis/digest (internal): every round answered in the window, grouped by person, each with its audit; the reviewer's own questions excluded

A reply to anyone who writes goes at once — never a draft for approval (Chad 10-19: 'if someone asks a question of Anis, they should get an immediate answer'); the engagement rules still decide in deliver(). A stale 10-08 test draft that the daily digest kept listing was discarded
An SLP job cancelled at SLP while the item is still wanted is forgotten and a new one started (the Greek New Testament looped on its cancelled job)

TRUNCATED BOOKS caught by the book's own apparatus — the highest page its contents point to, its index cites, its printed page numbers reach, against the PDF's length (ported from SearchLayerPDF's completeness.js, same tests; Chad 10-19 via the SLP session: 'so we do not accidentally think we have a book when we do not'). Checked for every offer (scouts, folder sweeps) and at intake (a text layer's first/last 20 pages; OCR Markdown's printed page labels) — a suspect copy goes to the acquire list with the evidence, never imported as the book. SLP's new awaiting_approval status: Dewey's own page gate already decided, so the job is approved once and read
'Put it on the acquire list' — an item that is only part of a book goes on the to-buy list with its copy kept as evidence (Chad 10-19)

ONLY A WHOLE COPY IS OFFERED (Chad 10-19: 'do not propose books that are incomplete. That is a trap'): a contents/index/appendix/excerpt/sample file, preview wording, a 'book' of a few thousand words, a PDF far shorter than its edition — passed over; the scout searches on for a whole copy, and an incomplete copy only puts the work on the ACQUIRE list ('such books might inform us of the existence of the actual book'); same for folder-sweep offers
The Review popup shows a document's total size (a PDF's pages, a text's words) and loads its whole text as you scroll

The Review popup shows a document's WHOLE text (the first 4,000 characters read as a cut-off book — Chad 10-19: 'I don't want to reject a book because it is not complete'); the folder sweep waits out the key's hourly limit instead of recording 429s, and re-checks erred files on resume

Folder-sweep finds become OFFERS (dewey-offer-paths: each missing file checked again, appraised, offered under Found with its verdict and nearest library copy — never imported unasked); the sweep skips helper files (.debug, .sample, images)
The spot-check always reads PAGE 1 (the title page — skipped, a body sentence or the author's name became the title) and spreads the rest to the last page
A title must look like one (capital start, ≤ 20 words, no trailing comma, mostly capitalised) — a body sentence was taken as the title after the author line

A title page's first line that is a known author is the author, not the title ('MOOJAN MOMEN'); metadata lines skipped; bahai-library pilgrim notes shelve as Bahá'í › Pilgrim Notes (one went to Christian › Mysticism by its text)

A linked Word file keeps its type (a .docx saved as .html read as junk — 'not usable text'); a generic lead-in before the colon ('Pilgrim Notes: …') is not a work's name for the twin guard (two different pilgrim notes held as twins)

ARCHIVE — unsearchable documents that may have value later (illegible handwriting, unreadable scans) are kept: the original on the NAS with its record, out of the searchable library; 'Archive it' answer in Review, also for an imported document (withdrawn, reversible). Media plan: transcript + link for now (Chad 10-19)
The title a work was SOUGHT under is kept; a re-scout looks for the work, not its copy's appraised title
'a summary' / 'meditation on' are derivative

Precision on the real library's confusables — a derivative work (study guide, notes, commentary, companion, homage…) is not the work unless asked; words in front of the work's title count against it; a one-word title must be the whole title (unless it is the title written together)

The librarian's TITLE INDEX — every library title folded to its main title (no diacritics/apostrophes, subtitle, volume, edition, generic prefix like Táríkh-i-/Kitáb-i-/The) and matched fuzzily (consonant skeleton for transliteration, word match for order and slips, subtitles indexed too, authors folded); used by every holdings check. Chad 10-19: Dewey missed Ẓuhúru'l-Ḥaqq (nine held volumes, asked as 'Táríkh-i-Ẓuhúru'l-Ḥaqq'), The Dawn-Breakers (long subtitle) and the Summa (Theologiae/Theologica) — 'our librarian API cannot be so weak as to miss slight variations in title'. dewey-title-check report runs a battery against the real library
A list's alternative title in brackets is searched too when nothing downloadable turned up (The New History of the Báb is catalogued as The Táríkh-i-Jadíd)
Held is also checked by the main title (a list's long subtitle hid The Dawn-Breakers); an offer whose copy reads as another work says so

The first pulse's mistakes — a loose title match imported two wrong works (sameWork: the found main title must BEGIN with the sought one, hyphenated words whole, a companion/commentary is not the work; auto-add also requires the copy's appraised title to be the sought one); a channel that could not be asked (Google Books quota, dead gutendex) is logged NOT searched instead of 'nothing found'; Gutenberg via its own OPDS catalogue, multi-volume works gathered into one copy; archive.org searched for downloadable copies separately and by title when the author is catalogued otherwise; Wikisource channel; lists ask for book-length works only and fall back to a quicker research run; retry param re-scouts to-buy/lead items

2026-10-18.description: Supersets embed the whole held text
Downloads strip the internal sentence markers (⁅s1⁆…⁅/s1⁆) — every sentence of marked documents (Arabic, Persian, French) came out wrapped; found by the Dewey benchmark

No placeholder titles — a scan appraised from unreadable pages ('… not legible in the excerpts') is re-appraised from its OCR text; dewey-retitle report proposes real titles (printed, or an archival supplied title in brackets) for the 17 already imported
Media collection plan (lectures per tradition) — draft with Chad's three decisions
A held work inside a larger file of ours (held book + new chapters, a fuller edition) is PARTIAL, not same — the new material was being skipped (benchmark P10: 6 of 6)

The daily pulse — once a day the scouts run (bahai-library collection by collection, pilgrim notes first; important Bahá'í publications; the core works of the next tradition in rotation) and ADD the most important finds themselves (importance ≥ 4, not held by text, in scope, recommended; ≤ 15 a day; intake guards still apply). Scouts — the library advisor (core works of each tradition, researched) and the Bahá'í scout (every bahai-library collection via RIS — pilgrim notes first — and researched lists of important publications): held? → every channel searched (bahai-library page, archive.org incl. borrow-only, Google Books, HathiTrust, Gutenberg, Open Library, bahai.works, the open web; never shadow libraries) → a copy downloaded, its text checked against the library, appraised and OFFERED with where it came from

A job SLP failed on its own side (expired source link: 'fetch source … HTTP 401' at page 323/342) is reprocessed once under the same id, keeping pages already read; a cancelled SLP job ends the wait (SLP's DELETE now cancels active jobs)

Declining stops OCR — a decline cancels the item's open SLP job (DELETE), a run polling SLP notices the decline within a poll, cancels and never fetches or uses the result, queued runs of a declined item are skipped; a book scan far shorter than the published book (< 25% of its pages) is held for a person BEFORE paying for OCR

A book's PDF is checked against its published length — Open Library / Google Books page count looked up when the item has no research (ingest-folder books); short by pages AND words (two-up scans allowed) → held for a person, not added

One OCR run per item — the OCR loop skips items already queued (a Review answer's run has a priority flag, so enqueue's dedupe missed it: four items queued twice) and a second concurrent run of one item is skipped, never paying SLP twice
Completeness report also compares each library document's words with its source text's

Only the WHOLE document is imported — SLP/OCR text must reach the PDF's last pages (page markers ≥85% of the PDF's own page count, text on most pages) and our own sampled late pages must be in it; checked against the PDF's page count, never SLP's; intake also holds previews ('not shown in this preview'), PDFs far shorter than the published book, and sends a text layer that stops early to full OCR; dewey-completeness report audits what is already imported

Loading column says plainly 'Loaded — in the library and searchable' (text + BM25) and clears a loaded book after an hour, active work first; Wanted tab lists only books still sought (no source) — items at OCR or loading were shown twice
Review answers — no 'add it' for a scan without accepted text (it only went back to OCR); OCR that matched our own read under 30% recommends running OCR again, not using it

/dewey page — thread opens at the latest message (no scroll-through); missing column hides works now held (a real document of the same title) and repeated titles; loading column shows stage chips + live OCR pages; 'Needs a person' gets a Review popup (view the original, read Dewey's text, answer: add it / use OCR text / run OCR again / decline) — GET items/:id/review, GET items/:id/file, POST items/:id/resolve; a person's 'add it' waives the fragment, twin, recheck and page-limit guards

OCR refresh — an imported document takes SLP's improved result for the same job when it agrees with our own text, re-imported in place; a scan's OCR text is checked against the library before import (one Sears letter came in from two files)
Every SearchLayerPDF request retried on a network error (four jobs ended 'fetch failed' — tower's uplink, not the files); a resumed job still awaiting its upload is uploaded
A job SLP reported failed is re-polled under its id (SLP completes failed jobs later); the import log names the vision transcription instead of 'SLP job undefined'
A re-run SLP job is re-fetched under the same id (current output + receipt), saved copy as fallback; ops runs with params.priority go first in their lane

Real-word measure is Unicode-aware (Bahá'u'lláh, Kitáb-i-Íqán counted as noise), all-caps headings and hyphen-joined parts count, numbers/page refs/initials not judged; garbled thresholds recalibrated (clean 0.98–0.99, garbled 0.79–0.84); inspector no longer counts headings before numbered lists, TOC lines or repeated endnote citations
